exposure: Mode of birth (caesarean section vs. natural)
cohort: The study included 104 preterm infants with a gestational age of less than 34 weeks who received treatment in a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU).
finding: The study found associations between severe respiratory disorders, twin status, neonatal seizures, and mode of birth with altered levels of dopamine, b-endorphin, and serotonin in preterm infants.
mod_finding: Serotonin level was significantly higher in neonates born by caesarean section compared to those born naturally.
cross-section timing: Measurements were taken during the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) stay of the preterm infants.
